# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

"description": "Stuck In Development Test Cases → recover (check PR, route to Rework/Review/Backlog)",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND status in ('{status.IN_DEVELOPMENT:In Development}') AND updated <= -15m",
          "configFile": "agents/recover_stuck_test_case.json",
          "localExecution": true,
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "In Rework Test Cases → trigger pr_test_automation_rework",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND status in ('{status.IN_REWORK:In Rework}')",
          "configFile": "agents/pr_test_automation_rework.json",
          "skipIfLabel": "sm_test_rework_triggered",
          "addLabel": "sm_test_rework_triggered",
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "In Review Test Cases → trigger pr_test_automation_review",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND ({stage.IN_REVIEW_PASSED:In Review - Passed} OR {stage.IN_REVIEW_FAILED:In Review - Failed}) AND (labels is EMPTY OR labels NOT IN ('pr_approved'))",
          "configFile": "agents/pr_test_automation_review.json",
          "skipIfLabel": "sm_test_review_triggered",
          "addLabel": "sm_test_review_triggered",
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "In Review Test Cases with dirty PR → move to In Rework",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND ({stage.IN_REVIEW_PASSED:In Review - Passed} OR {stage.IN_REVIEW_FAILED:In Review - Failed})",
          "configFile": "agents/recover_dirty_review_test_case.json",
          "localExecution": true,
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "Failed Test Cases → create or link bug (single, disabled by default — use bulk_bugs_creation instead)",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND {stage.FAILED:Failed}",
          "configFile": "agents/bug_creation.json",
          "skipIfLabel": "sm_bug_creation_triggered",
          "addLabel": "sm_bug_creation_triggered",
          "limit": 5,
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "Backlog / To Do / Ready For Development Test Cases → In Development + automate",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND status in ('{status.BACKLOG:Backlog}', '{status.TODO:To Do}', '{status.READY_FOR_DEVELOPMENT:Ready For Development}')",
          "targetStatus": "In Development",
          "configFile": "agents/test_case_automation.json",
          "skipIfLabel": "sm_test_automation_triggered",
          "addLabel": "sm_test_automation_triggered",
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "Bug To Fix Tickets → all linked Bugs Done → move to Backlog / Ready For Testing",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case', 'Story') AND {stage.BUG_TO_FIX:Bug To Fix}",
          "configFile": "agents/bug_to_fix_check.json",
          "skipIfLabel": "sm_bug_to_fix_check_triggered",
          "localExecution": true,
          "enabled": true
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

# gh-1027: conflict-rework: already-reported DIRTY PRs must not consume the per-tick limit (structural)

## Description

Follow-up from #1025 (review thread on PR #1026): `conflict-rework` shipped the limit 1 → 5 mitigation — an already-reported DIRTY PR still consumes a per-tick query slot, so the starvation class returns once 5+ already-reported DIRTY PRs park ahead of unreported ones, and each still costs a `github_get_pr_comments` fetch.

## Fix
Make already-reported candidates not consume the rule limit: scan candidates until `limit` *actionable* ones are processed, with a bounded scan. `smAgent.js` already detects `alreadyReported` inside the action before doing any work — the cheapest structural shape is a query-side marker filter for this rule (comments fetch moves from action to source filter) or an over-scan budget in the rule loop.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A tick with N already-reported DIRTY PRs still evaluates the (N+1)-th unreported one in the same tick.
- [ ] Marker dedup (once-per-head report) unchanged; gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

# gh-1027: conflict-rework: already-reported DIRTY PRs must not consume the per-tick limit (structural)

## Description

Follow-up from #1025 (review thread on PR #1026): `conflict-rework` shipped the limit 1 → 5 mitigation — an already-reported DIRTY PR still consumes a per-tick query slot, so the starvation class returns once 5+ already-reported DIRTY PRs park ahead of unreported ones, and each still costs a `github_get_pr_comments` fetch.

## Fix
Make already-reported candidates not consume the rule limit: scan candidates until `limit` *actionable* ones are processed, with a bounded scan. `smAgent.js` already detects `alreadyReported` inside the action before doing any work — the cheapest structural shape is a query-side marker filter for this rule (comments fetch moves from action to source filter) or an over-scan budget in the rule loop.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A tick with N already-reported DIRTY PRs still evaluates the (N+1)-th unreported one in the same tick.
- [ ] Marker dedup (once-per-head report) unchanged; gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

# gh-1027: conflict-rework: already-reported DIRTY PRs must not consume the per-tick limit (structural)

## Description

Follow-up from #1025 (review thread on PR #1026): `conflict-rework` shipped the limit 1 → 5 mitigation — an already-reported DIRTY PR still consumes a per-tick query slot, so the starvation class returns once 5+ already-reported DIRTY PRs park ahead of unreported ones, and each still costs a `github_get_pr_comments` fetch.

## Fix
Make already-reported candidates not consume the rule limit: scan candidates until `limit` *actionable* ones are processed, with a bounded scan. `smAgent.js` already detects `alreadyReported` inside the action before doing any work — the cheapest structural shape is a query-side marker filter for this rule (comments fetch moves from action to source filter) or an over-scan budget in the rule loop.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A tick with N already-reported DIRTY PRs still evaluates the (N+1)-th unreported one in the same tick.
- [ ] Marker dedup (once-per-head report) unchanged; gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

"description": "Stuck In Development Test Cases → recover (check PR, route to Rework/Review/Backlog)",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND status in ('{status.IN_DEVELOPMENT:In Development}') AND updated <= -15m",
          "configFile": "agents/recover_stuck_test_case.json",
          "localExecution": true,
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "In Rework Test Cases → trigger pr_test_automation_rework",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND status in ('{status.IN_REWORK:In Rework}')",
          "configFile": "agents/pr_test_automation_rework.json",
          "skipIfLabel": "sm_test_rework_triggered",
          "addLabel": "sm_test_rework_triggered",
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "In Review Test Cases → trigger pr_test_automation_review",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND ({stage.IN_REVIEW_PASSED:In Review - Passed} OR {stage.IN_REVIEW_FAILED:In Review - Failed}) AND (labels is EMPTY OR labels NOT IN ('pr_approved'))",
          "configFile": "agents/pr_test_automation_review.json",
          "skipIfLabel": "sm_test_review_triggered",
          "addLabel": "sm_test_review_triggered",
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "In Review Test Cases with dirty PR → move to In Rework",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND ({stage.IN_REVIEW_PASSED:In Review - Passed} OR {stage.IN_REVIEW_FAILED:In Review - Failed})",
          "configFile": "agents/recover_dirty_review_test_case.json",
          "localExecution": true,
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "Failed Test Cases → create or link bug (single, disabled by default — use bulk_bugs_creation instead)",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND {stage.FAILED:Failed}",
          "configFile": "agents/bug_creation.json",
          "skipIfLabel": "sm_bug_creation_triggered",
          "addLabel": "sm_bug_creation_triggered",
          "limit": 5,
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "Backlog / To Do / Ready For Development Test Cases → In Development + automate",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case') AND status in ('{status.BACKLOG:Backlog}', '{status.TODO:To Do}', '{status.READY_FOR_DEVELOPMENT:Ready For Development}')",
          "targetStatus": "In Development",
          "configFile": "agents/test_case_automation.json",
          "skipIfLabel": "sm_test_automation_triggered",
          "addLabel": "sm_test_automation_triggered",
          "enabled": true
        },
        {
          "description": "Bug To Fix Tickets → all linked Bugs Done → move to Backlog / Ready For Testing",
          "jql": "project = {jiraProject} AND issuetype in ('Test Case', 'Story') AND {stage.BUG_TO_FIX:Bug To Fix}",
          "configFile": "agents/bug_to_fix_check.json",
          "skipIfLabel": "sm_bug_to_fix_check_triggered",
          "localExecution": true,
          "enabled": true
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

# gh-1027: conflict-rework: already-reported DIRTY PRs must not consume the per-tick limit (structural)

## Description

Follow-up from #1025 (review thread on PR #1026): `conflict-rework` shipped the limit 1 → 5 mitigation — an already-reported DIRTY PR still consumes a per-tick query slot, so the starvation class returns once 5+ already-reported DIRTY PRs park ahead of unreported ones, and each still costs a `github_get_pr_comments` fetch.

## Fix
Make already-reported candidates not consume the rule limit: scan candidates until `limit` *actionable* ones are processed, with a bounded scan. `smAgent.js` already detects `alreadyReported` inside the action before doing any work — the cheapest structural shape is a query-side marker filter for this rule (comments fetch moves from action to source filter) or an over-scan budget in the rule loop.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A tick with N already-reported DIRTY PRs still evaluates the (N+1)-th unreported one in the same tick.
- [ ] Marker dedup (once-per-head report) unchanged; gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

# gh-1027: conflict-rework: already-reported DIRTY PRs must not consume the per-tick limit (structural)

## Description

Follow-up from #1025 (review thread on PR #1026): `conflict-rework` shipped the limit 1 → 5 mitigation — an already-reported DIRTY PR still consumes a per-tick query slot, so the starvation class returns once 5+ already-reported DIRTY PRs park ahead of unreported ones, and each still costs a `github_get_pr_comments` fetch.

## Fix
Make already-reported candidates not consume the rule limit: scan candidates until `limit` *actionable* ones are processed, with a bounded scan. `smAgent.js` already detects `alreadyReported` inside the action before doing any work — the cheapest structural shape is a query-side marker filter for this rule (comments fetch moves from action to source filter) or an over-scan budget in the rule loop.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A tick with N already-reported DIRTY PRs still evaluates the (N+1)-th unreported one in the same tick.
- [ ] Marker dedup (once-per-head report) unchanged; gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

# gh-1027: conflict-rework: already-reported DIRTY PRs must not consume the per-tick limit (structural)

## Description

Follow-up from #1025 (review thread on PR #1026): `conflict-rework` shipped the limit 1 → 5 mitigation — an already-reported DIRTY PR still consumes a per-tick query slot, so the starvation class returns once 5+ already-reported DIRTY PRs park ahead of unreported ones, and each still costs a `github_get_pr_comments` fetch.

## Fix
Make already-reported candidates not consume the rule limit: scan candidates until `limit` *actionable* ones are processed, with a bounded scan. `smAgent.js` already detects `alreadyReported` inside the action before doing any work — the cheapest structural shape is a query-side marker filter for this rule (comments fetch moves from action to source filter) or an over-scan budget in the rule loop.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A tick with N already-reported DIRTY PRs still evaluates the (N+1)-th unreported one in the same tick.
- [ ] Marker dedup (once-per-head report) unchanged; gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

Now I understand the architecture. The plan: implement a query-side marker filter for the conflict-rework rule.

Key considerations:
1. The marker filter needs to fetch comments per candidate DIRTY PR — but only those matching the rule's query. To avoid the query returning `limit + reserve` candidates (where already-reported ones eat the slice), the filter must scan candidates and return up to `limit` *actionable* (not-already-reported) ones, with a bounded scan.

2. Important: `alreadyReported` check in the action is still needed? If the source filter removes already-reported ones, the action's `alreadyReported` branch handles the gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when label absent). Wait — the self-heal IS the point of the alreadyReported branch. If we filter out already-reported candidates at query time, the self-heal never runs! The AC says "gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged."

Hmm. So the self-heal must keep running for already-reported PRs whose linked issue lacks agent:rework. But if the query filters them out, the self-heal is lost.

Options:

# gh-1027: conflict-rework: already-reported DIRTY PRs must not consume the per-tick limit (structural)

## Description

Follow-up from #1025 (review thread on PR #1026): `conflict-rework` shipped the limit 1 → 5 mitigation — an already-reported DIRTY PR still consumes a per-tick query slot, so the starvation class returns once 5+ already-reported DIRTY PRs park ahead of unreported ones, and each still costs a `github_get_pr_comments` fetch.

## Fix
Make already-reported candidates not consume the rule limit: scan candidates until `limit` *actionable* ones are processed, with a bounded scan. `smAgent.js` already detects `alreadyReported` inside the action before doing any work — the cheapest structural shape is a query-side marker filter for this rule (comments fetch moves from action to source filter) or an over-scan budget in the rule loop.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A tick with N already-reported DIRTY PRs still evaluates the (N+1)-th unreported one in the same tick.
- [ ] Marker dedup (once-per-head report) unchanged; gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

Now I understand the architecture. The plan: implement a query-side marker filter for the conflict-rework rule.

Key considerations:
1. The marker filter needs to fetch comments per candidate DIRTY PR — but only those matching the rule's query. To avoid the query returning `limit + reserve` candidates (where already-reported ones eat the slice), the filter must scan candidates and return up to `limit` *actionable* (not-already-reported) ones, with a bounded scan.

2. Important: `alreadyReported` check in the action is still needed? If the source filter removes already-reported ones, the action's `alreadyReported` branch handles the gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when label absent). Wait — the self-heal IS the point of the alreadyReported branch. If we filter out already-reported candidates at query time, the self-heal never runs! The AC says "gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged."

Hmm. So the self-heal must keep running for already-reported PRs whose linked issue lacks agent:rework. But if the query filters them out, the self-heal is lost.

Options:
- The query-side filter removes already-reported candidates from the *limit accounting* but the rule loop still needs to process them for self-heal... Actually re-read the gh-683 self-heal: it's a recovery path — a marker present but label absent. That's a rare corpse state. The ticket says "gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged."

Alternative approach: over-scan budget in the rule loop. The engine loop currently breaks when `processedKeys.length >= effectiveLimit`. For the conflict_rework action, already-reported candidates push processedKeys. Change: for conflict_rework, don't push processedKeys for already-reported ones? But then the loop would keep scanning all tickets — unbounded. Need a bounded scan: scan candidates until `limit` actionable ones are processed, with a bounded scan (e.g., scan at most limit + K extra, or scan the full returned list but cap the number of already-reported skips).

Hmm, but where does the fetch cost come in? The action fetches comments for each scanned candidate regardless.

Wait, let me reconsider. The two structural options from the ticket:
1. Query-side marker filter: comments fetch moves from action to source filter. The source filter scans candidates, skipping already-reported ones WITHOUT counting toward limit. Bounded scan. The action then doesn't need to fetch comments... but the action still needs `alreadyReported` for the self-heal. Hmm, but if the filter guarantees only unreported candidates arrive, the self-heal would never trigger. UNLESS the filter only filters "reported AND healthy" — i.e., a candidate is dropped only if alreadyReported AND the self-heal condition doesn't apply. But the self-heal check requires resolving machine author + linked issue + label state — expensive per candidate in the query.

Alternative: keep the self-heal in the action but make it reachable: the query filter keeps already-reported candidates that need self-heal... too complex.

2. Over-scan budget in the rule loop: for the conflict_rework rule, the loop skips already-reported candidates without consuming limit slots, up to a bounded over-scan (e.g., 2× limit + reserve). The self-heal stays in the action unchanged. This preserves all behavior — AC2 trivialy satisfied since the action code path is untouched except the limit accounting.

Option 2 is much simpler and satisfies both ACs. The per-candidate comments fetch cost remains, but that's inherent — you must read the marker to know it's already reported. Actually could we reduce fetches? No — detecting alreadyReported requires the comments fetch. The ticket complains about the fetch cost as context, but the primary starvation is the limit. The acceptance criteria only mention the starvation.

# gh-1027: conflict-rework: already-reported DIRTY PRs must not consume the per-tick limit (structural)

## Description

Follow-up from #1025 (review thread on PR #1026): `conflict-rework` shipped the limit 1 → 5 mitigation — an already-reported DIRTY PR still consumes a per-tick query slot, so the starvation class returns once 5+ already-reported DIRTY PRs park ahead of unreported ones, and each still costs a `github_get_pr_comments` fetch.

## Fix
Make already-reported candidates not consume the rule limit: scan candidates until `limit` *actionable* ones are processed, with a bounded scan. `smAgent.js` already detects `alreadyReported` inside the action before doing any work — the cheapest structural shape is a query-side marker filter for this rule (comments fetch moves from action to source filter) or an over-scan budget in the rule loop.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A tick with N already-reported DIRTY PRs still evaluates the (N+1)-th unreported one in the same tick.
- [ ] Marker dedup (once-per-head report) unchanged; gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

A cancelled required check is never a verdict: the sweep skips cancelled conclusions by design and fail-validation owns red, so this rule cannot fight them — it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, it only re-runs GitHub Actions runs. GitHub PR: armed (ai_validating) or latched (ai_validated) head whose REQUIRED check contexts (rule.requiredContexts, branch protection here: static/gate/agents-gate; in fa the kicker's sm-liveness/head-completeness) concluded CANCELLED — the kicker cancel-loop death: every silent-refresh push queued a new kicker run and the pending one was superseded (cancelled) in the shared concurrency group, required contexts died CANCELLED on fresh heads, PRs BLOCKED until manual reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone). # gh-1027: conflict-rework: already-reported DIRTY PRs must not consume the per-tick limit (structural)

## Description

Follow-up from #1025 (review thread on PR #1026): `conflict-rework` shipped the limit 1 → 5 mitigation — an already-reported DIRTY PR still consumes a per-tick query slot, so the starvation class returns once 5+ already-reported DIRTY PRs park ahead of unreported ones, and each still costs a `github_get_pr_comments` fetch.

## Fix
Make already-reported candidates not consume the rule limit: scan candidates until `limit` *actionable* ones are processed, with a bounded scan. `smAgent.js` already detects `alreadyReported` inside the action before doing any work — the cheapest structural shape is a query-side marker filter for this rule (comments fetch moves from action to source filter) or an over-scan budget in the rule loop.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A tick with N already-reported DIRTY PRs still evaluates the (N+1)-th unreported one in the same tick.
- [ ] Marker dedup (once-per-head report) unchanged; gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

# gh-1027: conflict-rework: already-reported DIRTY PRs must not consume the per-tick limit (structural)

## Description

Follow-up from #1025 (review thread on PR #1026): `conflict-rework` shipped the limit 1 → 5 mitigation — an already-reported DIRTY PR still consumes a per-tick query slot, so the starvation class returns once 5+ already-reported DIRTY PRs park ahead of unreported ones, and each still costs a `github_get_pr_comments` fetch.

## Fix
Make already-reported candidates not consume the rule limit: scan candidates until `limit` *actionable* ones are processed, with a bounded scan. `smAgent.js` already detects `alreadyReported` inside the action before doing any work — the cheapest structural shape is a query-side marker filter for this rule (comments fetch moves from action to source filter) or an over-scan budget in the rule loop.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A tick with N already-reported DIRTY PRs still evaluates the (N+1)-th unreported one in the same tick.
- [ ] Marker dedup (once-per-head report) unchanged; gh-683 self-heal (re-arm when the label is absent) unchanged.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

sm_github.json:12:          "description": "RULE ORDER (dmtools-agents#682, live fa#1202/#1203 2026-10-03 23:05–23:57, still reproducing 2026-10-04 06:21–06:22): runs FIRST, ahead of merge-validated AND sweep-stale-validating (whose relative order is a documented #637 invariant — this rule preserves it by prefixing, never interleaving). A cancelled required check is never a verdict: the sweep skips cancelled conclusions by design and fail-validation owns red, so this rule cannot fight them — it never touches labels and never dispatches workflows, it only re-runs GitHub Actions runs. GitHub PR: armed (ai_validating) or latched (ai_validated) head whose REQUIRED check contexts (rule.requiredContexts, branch protection here: static/gate/agents-gate; in fa the kicker's sm-liveness/head-completeness) concluded CANCELLED — the kicker cancel-loop death: every silent-refresh push queued a new kicker run and the pending one was superseded (cancelled) in the shared concurrency group, required contexts died CANCELLED on fresh heads, PRs BLOCKED until manual reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone). CANCELLED is read with branch-protection semantics: the LATEST check run per context is the verdict — a stale cancel under a fresh green re-stamp does NOT act (#695 review fix). GitHub PR: armed (ai_validating) or latched (ai_validated) head whose REQUIRED check contexts (rule.requiredContexts, branch protection here: static/gate/agents-gate; in fa the kicker's sm-liveness/head-completeness) concluded CANCELLED — the kicker cancel-loop death: every silent-refresh push queued a new kicker run and the pending one was superseded (cancelled) in the shared concurrency group, required contexts died CANCELLED on fresh heads, PRs BLOCKED until manual reruns (2 dead zones + 2 manual reruns on 2026-10-03 alone). CANCELLED is read with branch-protection semantics: the LATEST check run per context is the verdict — a stale cancel under a fresh green re-stamp does NOT act (#695 review fix).
